item.title: High Carbon Steel Needle Nose Pliers — Precision Tip for 3D Printing & DIY
item.description: Spec – Value Material – High Carbon Steel jaws and body Jaw Type – Smooth, pointed needle nose Grip – Comfort grip handles Primary Use – 3D printing support removal, filament handling, bed maintenance Jaw Surface – Smooth (non-serrated, won't scratch printed surfaces or damage filament) Suitable For – Support removal, purge pulling, failed print cleanup, insert placement Handy Tips Support removal made easy — The pointed needle nose tip gets into tight cavities and undercuts where fingers can't reach, making removal of tree and grid supports from intricate prints clean and controlled without damaging the model surface. Pulling purge and ooze strings — Use these to grab and pull filament purge blobs, stringing, and ooze from the nozzle before a print starts — far more effective and safer than fingers near a hot hotend. Heat set insert placement — The smooth jaws are ideal for holding and positioning brass heat set inserts above holes before pressing them in with a soldering iron, keeping fingers safely away from the heat. Clearing blocked nozzles — When performing a cold pull or removing a partial clog, needle nose pliers give the controlled grip needed to pull filament cleanly through the hotend without snapping it mid-pull. Bed clip and spring management — Removing and repositioning binder clips, PEI sheet clips, or glass bed retaining springs is significantly easier and safer with needle nose pliers, especially on enclosed printers with limited hand clearance. First layer peel assist — For prints that bond very firmly to the bed, use the tip to carefully get under a corner edge and begin the peel without flexing or scratching the build plate surface. Never use on a live heated bed — The high carbon steel body is conductive and transfers heat. Always allow the bed and hotend to cool before using metal pliers near heating elements, thermistor wires, or bed terminals.

item.title: Inline Fuse Holder with ATC/ATO Blade Fuse Set (10A–40A) for 12V Systems
item.description: Spec – Value Fuse Type – ATC/ATO Standard Blade Fuse Included Fuse Ratings – 10A, 15A, 20A, 25A, 30A, 40A System Voltage – 12V DC Holder Wire Gauge – Typically 14AWG (check product) Connection Type – Inline (series with load wire) Waterproofing – Cover/cap included (splash resistant) Suitable For – Cars, trucks, bakkies, boats, caravans, solar systems Fuse Standard – ATC (non-time delay) / ATO (open element) Handy Tips Always fuse at the source — Mount the inline fuse holder as close to the positive battery terminal or power source as possible (within 300mm ideally). This protects the entire length of wire from a short circuit, not just the load end. Match the fuse to the wire, not just the load — The fuse rating must not exceed what your wire gauge can safely carry. 14AWG wire is rated for approximately 15A continuous — using a 40A fuse on thin wire defeats the purpose of protection entirely. ATC vs ATO difference — Both ATC and ATO blade fuses are physically interchangeable in this holder. ATC fuses have a closed body for better vibration resistance, making them preferable in vehicles. ATO fuses have an open body allowing visual inspection of the element without removal. 12V DC only — This holder is rated for 12V DC automotive systems. Do not use on 240V AC mains circuits — blade fuses are not rated for mains voltage and present a serious shock and fire hazard if misapplied. Use for solar and caravan systems — Inline fuse holders are ideal for 12V solar setups, adding protection between your charge controller, battery, and DC loads such as lights, pumps, and inverters. Check the cap regularly — The protective cap keeps moisture and corrosion off the fuse contacts. In marine or outdoor environments inspect the cap and contacts every few months and apply a light coat of dielectric grease to prevent oxidation. Upgrade the wire if going above 20A — For the 25A, 30A, and 40A fuses to be meaningful, ensure your wiring is upgraded accordingly. 40A loads require at least 8AWG wire to avoid voltage drop and heat buildup over any meaningful cable run length.

item.title: DTS61R 6x6mm Low-Profile Tactile Push Button Switch — Momentary SPST PCB Mount (Red) - Pack of 5
item.description: Spec – Value Type – Tactile Momentary Push Button Series – DTS61R Switch Circuit – SPST Normally Open (NO) / 4 Terminal Electrical Rating – 50mA @ 12V DC Actuation Force – 260gf Actuator Style – Push Button Termination – PCB Through-Hole Case Dimensions – 6mm (L) x 6mm (W) x 4.3mm (H) Lever/Button Size – 0.8mm Colour – Red Handy Tips Low-profile design — At only 4.3mm total height with a 0.8mm actuator, the DTS61R sits extremely close to the PCB surface — ideal for slim enclosures, wearables, and space-constrained builds where the taller DTS65R (9.5mm) would not fit. 4-pin through-hole layout — Like other 6x6mm tactile switches, the 4 legs form 2 electrically connected pairs. Pins 1&2 are one side of the switch and pins 3&4 are the other, giving excellent mechanical stability on the PCB while only requiring one pair per side for a basic SPST connection. Normally Open by default — The switch is open at rest and closes only while pressed. For microcontroller use, connect one side to your GPIO pin and the other to GND, and enable the internal pull-up resistor in your code to avoid a floating input state. Debounce in software — All mechanical tactile switches produce contact bounce on press and release. Add a 10–50ms debounce delay in Arduino, ESPHome, or MicroPython to prevent false multiple triggers from a single button press. 0.8mm actuator requires direct PCB access — The very short 0.8mm actuator height means this switch is best used where the button is accessed directly through a small panel cutout flush with the PCB, or paired with a custom 3D printed actuator extension to make it reachable through a thicker enclosure wall. 50mA rating is signal-level only — This switch is designed strictly for logic and signal switching. Do not use it to directly switch motors, solenoids, or LED strips — use it as a trigger input to a microcontroller GPIO, MOSFET, or relay instead. Soldering tip — The low-profile body sits very close to the PCB, making heat dissipation through the legs slower. Solder quickly with a clean, well-tinned iron tip to avoid prolonged heat exposure that can warp the casing or bind the actuator mechanism.

item.title: L9110S Dual DC Motor Driver Module — 2x 800mA for Arduino, ESP32 & Robotics
item.description: Spec – Value Driver IC – L9110S Supply Voltage – 2.5V–12V DC Motor Operating Voltage – 2.5V–12V DC Maximum Current Per Channel – 800mA continuous Number of Channels – 2 (dual motor) Motor Types Supported – 2x DC motors or 1x 4-wire 2-phase stepper motor PCB Size – 28mm x 21mm (ultra-compact) Mounting Holes – Yes, 3mm diameter Control Interface – 4x GPIO pins (IA1, IB1, IA2, IB2) Logic Voltage – 3.3V and 5V compatible Power Indicator – Yes (onboard LED) Output Connector – 4-pin green screw terminal Compatible With – Arduino, ESP32, Raspberry Pi, PLC Pinout Reference 6-pin control header (black bent pin): Pin Label Function 1 VCC Power input 2.5V–12V 2 GND Ground 3 IA1 Motor A direction input 1 4 IB1 Motor A direction input 2 5 IA2 Motor B direction input 1 6 IB2 Motor B direction input 2 4-pin green screw terminal (motor outputs): Terminal Label Function 1 OA1 / OB1 Motor A output (either wire) 2 OA2 / OB2 Motor B output (either wire) Handy Tips Direction control truth table — For Motor A: IA1 HIGH + IB1 LOW = forward; IA1 LOW + IB1 HIGH = reverse; both LOW = coast/stop; both HIGH = brake. The same logic applies to IA2/IB2 for Motor B — no additional enable pin is needed. PWM speed control — Connect IA1 or IB1 to a PWM-capable GPIO pin and set the opposing pin LOW to control motor speed via duty cycle. This works on both Arduino ( analogWrite ) and ESP32 ( ledcWrite ) without any additional components. 3.3V logic compatible — The L9110S control inputs work reliably at 3.3V logic levels, making it directly compatible with ESP32, ESP8266, and Raspberry Pi GPIO pins without level shifting. Separate motor and logic power if needed — While VCC powers both the logic and motor driver from a single supply, for noise-sensitive applications consider decoupling with a 100µF electrolytic capacitor across the VCC and GND pins close to the module to absorb motor switching spikes. Stepper motor support — To drive a 4-wire 2-phase stepper motor, connect both coil pairs to OA and OB outputs and step through the IA1/IB1/IA2/IB2 pin sequence in your code. Standard full-step and half-step sequences apply — no additional library hardware is required. 800mA per channel is a continuous rating — Peak currents during motor startup or stall can exceed this significantly. For motors that stall frequently or draw high startup current, add a small heatsink or ensure adequate airflow over the IC to prevent thermal shutdown. Motor wire polarity determines direction — The screw terminal outputs have no fixed polarity — swapping the two wires on a DC motor reverses its physical direction relative to your control logic. Set your wiring first, then confirm direction in code before finalising your installation.

item.title: BMT Waterproof Ultrasonic Distance Sensor — 4.5m Range, 40kHz for Arduino & ESP32
item.description: Spec – Value Operating Voltage – 5V DC Quiescent Current – 5mA Working Current – 30mA Ultrasonic Frequency – 40kHz Maximum Range – 4.5m Blind Zone – 25cm minimum Resolution – ~0.5cm Detection Angle – Operating Temperature – -10°C to +70°C Storage Temperature – -20°C to +80°C Waterproofing – Yes (weatherproof transducer) Interface – Trig (TX) / Echo (RX) Wiring – VCC (+5V), Trig, Echo, GND Handy Tips Mind the 25cm blind zone — Objects closer than 25cm to the sensor face will not be detected reliably and may produce erratic or zero readings. Design your mounting position to ensure your nearest expected target is always beyond this minimum distance — critical for tank level sensing and obstacle avoidance applications. Distance calculation is straightforward — Trigger the sensor with a 10µs HIGH pulse on the Trig pin, then measure the duration of the HIGH pulse returned on the Echo pin in microseconds. Divide by 58 to get distance in centimetres (accounts for the speed of sound and the round-trip travel time). 5V logic — level shift for 3.3V microcontrollers — The Echo pin outputs a 5V signal. Connecting this directly to an ESP32 or Raspberry Pi GPIO pin (3.3V tolerant only) risks damaging the microcontroller. Use a simple voltage divider (1kΩ + 2kΩ) or a logic level shifter on the Echo line when using 3.3V systems. Waterproof transducer, not waterproof electronics — The ultrasonic transducer probe itself is weatherproof and can be mounted externally in rain or splash environments. However, if your module has a separate controller board, keep that board dry and protected inside an enclosure — only the probe head is sealed for outdoor exposure. Avoid highly absorptive surfaces — Soft materials such as foam, thick fabric, loose soil, and angled or irregular surfaces absorb or scatter ultrasonic energy rather than reflecting it cleanly back to the sensor. For best results, use on hard flat surfaces (water, concrete, metal, glass) that reflect sound efficiently. Add a timeout in your code — If no echo is received (target out of range or absorbed), the Echo pin can stay HIGH indefinitely and hang your code. Always set a maximum timeout in your pulse measurement function — typically 30ms, corresponding to the maximum 4.5m range round trip at the speed of sound. Separate power supply for stable readings — Ultrasonic sensors draw a brief current spike on each trigger pulse. Powering directly from a microcontroller's 5V pin alongside other peripherals can cause voltage dips that introduce jitter in readings. For best accuracy, power from a dedicated 5V rail or add a 100µF decoupling capacitor across the VCC and GND pins close to the sensor module.

item.title: BMT Flame Sensor Module — Digital & Analog Output, 760nm–1100nm for Arduino & ESP32
item.description: Spec – Value Spectral Range – 760nm–1100nm (near-infrared) Detection Angle – ~60 degrees Operating Voltage – 3.3V–5V DC Output Types – Analog (AO) + Digital (DO) Comparator IC – LM393 Detection Distance – Up to 0.8m (lighter flame) / further for larger flames Sensitivity – Adjustable via onboard trimmer potentiometer Indicators – Red (power) / Green (digital trigger) Mounting – Yes, onboard screw hole Compatible With – Arduino, ESP32, Raspberry Pi Typical Use – Flame detection, fire alarm, light sensing Handy Tips Two outputs for two use cases — The module provides both a digital output (DO) and an analog output (AO). Use the digital output for simple flame present/not-present triggering in alarm circuits, and the analog output when you need to measure relative flame intensity or proximity — for example to trigger different alarm levels at different distances. Adjust sensitivity with the onboard trimmer — The blue potentiometer controls the LM393 comparator threshold — turning it adjusts the point at which the digital output switches from HIGH to LOW. Start with the trimmer centred, then fine-tune in your actual environment to avoid false triggers from ambient light or sunlight. Sunlight and incandescent bulbs can cause false triggers — The 760nm–1100nm detection range overlaps significantly with sunlight and warm-white incandescent light output. In outdoor or brightly lit indoor environments, adjust the sensitivity trimmer to its least sensitive position and use the analog output with a software threshold rather than relying solely on the digital output. Digital output logic is inverted — When a flame is detected the digital output goes LOW (0), not HIGH. Account for this in your microcontroller code by triggering your alarm on a falling edge or a LOW state rather than a HIGH — a common source of confusion when first wiring up the module. Detection distance scales with flame size — The 0.8m detection distance is for a small lighter flame. A candle flame will trigger at slightly less, while a larger open flame such as a gas burner or fire can trigger the sensor from several metres away. Characterise the detection distance in your specific environment before setting alarm thresholds. Mount at an angle facing downward for fire detection — For fire alarm applications, angle the sensor face slightly downward toward the expected flame source rather than mounting horizontally. This keeps the sensor face away from dust accumulation on the IR lens and improves response to floor-level ignition sources. Pair with a buzzer or relay for a standalone alarm — The LM393 digital output can directly drive a small buzzer or the input of a relay module without any additional transistor or driver circuit, making it straightforward to build a completely self-contained flame alarm with just this module, a buzzer, and a 5V power supply.

item.title: BMT Line Tracking Obstacle Avoidance Sensor Module — 2–40cm Adjustable Range for Arduino & ESP32 Robots
item.description: Spec – Value Operating Voltage – 3.3V–5V DC Working Current – ≥20mA Operating Temperature – -10°C to +50°C Detection Distance – 2–40cm (adjustable) Effective Detection Angle – 35° Output Signal – TTL Digital (LOW = obstacle, HIGH = clear) Interface – 4-wire (- / + / S / EN) Sensitivity Adjustment – Multi-turn potentiometer PCB Size – 28mm x 23mm Compatible With – Arduino, ESP32, Raspberry Pi, BS2 Typical Use – Robot obstacle avoidance, edge detection, proximity sensing Handy Tips Output logic is inverted — LOW means obstacle detected — When an obstacle is present the signal pin (S) outputs LOW (0V), and HIGH when the path is clear. Account for this in your code by triggering your obstacle response on a LOW state or falling edge — the reverse of what many beginners initially expect. Use the EN pin to save power — The EN (enable) pin allows you to switch the sensor on and off from your microcontroller. In battery-powered robots, pulse EN HIGH only when a reading is needed rather than running the IR transmitter continuously — the IR LED draws significant current and disabling it between readings meaningfully extends battery life. Adjust range with the multi-turn potentiometer — Turn the trimmer clockwise to increase detection distance and anticlockwise to decrease it. Make adjustments in small increments and test against a white A4 sheet of paper at your target distance — white surfaces reflect IR well and give a consistent calibration reference. Surface colour and reflectivity affect range significantly — Dark or matte black surfaces absorb infrared and may only trigger at a fraction of the maximum 40cm range. Shiny or white surfaces reflect strongly and trigger at greater distances. Calibrate your sensitivity setting against the actual surface colours present in your robot's operating environment. Ambient light can cause false readings — Direct sunlight or strong incandescent lighting floods the IR receiver and can cause permanent false triggers regardless of obstacle presence. For outdoor or brightly lit environments, shield the sensor face from direct overhead light using a small 3D printed hood, or switch to a time-of-flight (ToF) sensor for better ambient light immunity. Minimum detection distance is 2cm — Objects closer than 2cm may not trigger the sensor reliably due to the geometry of the transmitter and receiver beams not overlapping at very short range. For applications requiring detection of very close obstacles, mount the sensor slightly recessed or angled outward, or use a separate short-range contact bumper switch. Ideal for line-following and edge detection too — Beyond obstacle avoidance, this sensor works well for line following (detecting the contrast between a dark line and a light floor) and table-edge detection (sensing the drop-off on a surface). Adjust the sensitivity trimmer to the minimum range needed for each application to reduce false triggers from background reflections.

item.title: HKD Slotted Optical Speed Sensor Module — 74HC14 Schmitt Trigger, TTL Output for Arduino & ESP32
item.description: Spec – Value Sensor Type – Slotted infrared optical (IR LED + NPN phototransistor) Schmitt Trigger IC – 74HC14 (hex inverting Schmitt trigger) Slot Width – 5.9mm Operating Voltage – 3.3V–5V DC Output Type – Digital TTL switch (LOW = beam interrupted, HIGH = beam clear) Output Form – Active LOW (0 = triggered, 1 = clear) Mounting – M3 screw holes at both ends Compatible With – Arduino, ESP32, Raspberry Pi Typical Use – Speed measurement, RPM counting, distance/position encoding Handy Tips Works with encoder / code wheels — Mount this sensor around a slotted encoder disc (code wheel) on a motor shaft or wheel axle. Each slot that passes through the beam generates one pulse on the output pin. Count pulses per second and divide by the number of slots on your disc to calculate RPM or surface speed accurately. Schmitt trigger gives clean, stable pulses — The onboard 74HC14 Schmitt trigger cleans up the raw phototransistor signal, eliminating the slow rise/fall edges and bounce that raw optical sensors produce. This makes it safe to connect directly to a microcontroller interrupt pin without additional filtering or debounce circuitry. Use hardware interrupts for accurate counting — Attach the output pin to a hardware interrupt-capable GPIO and count pulses in an ISR (Interrupt Service Routine). At higher RPMs the pulse rate can exceed what polling in a main loop can reliably capture — missed pulses directly translate to underreported speed readings. Output is active LOW — The output goes LOW when an opaque object interrupts the IR beam and returns HIGH when the beam is clear. In speed measurement applications this means each falling edge represents one slot passing through the sensor — trigger your interrupt on FALLING for the most consistent timing reference. Slot width limits maximum disc tooth size — The 5.9mm slot accommodates encoder disc teeth and flags up to approximately 5mm wide. Ensure your code wheel teeth are narrow enough to pass cleanly through the slot without touching the sensor body — physical contact will damage the sensor and produce erratic output. Transparent or translucent objects will not trigger — The sensor only triggers when the IR beam is fully interrupted by an opaque object. Clear acrylic, thin paper, and semi-transparent plastics may pass through the slot without reliably breaking the beam. Use a solid opaque encoder disc material such as black PLA, ABS, or metal for consistent triggering. M3 mounting holes allow precise alignment — Use both M3 mounting holes to secure the sensor rigidly to your chassis or bracket. Any flex or vibration in the sensor mounting will cause the encoder disc to drift within the slot, introducing timing jitter and inconsistent pulse widths that degrade speed measurement accuracy.

item.title: 2N2222A NPN General Purpose Transistor (TO-92) - 5 Pack
item.description: A convenient 5-pack of the 2N2222A NPN general-purpose transistor in the classic TO-92 package — one of the most widely used switching and amplification transistors in electronics. Ideal for hobby projects, prototyping and repairs where you want a few spares on hand. Spec – Value Pack Quantity – 5 transistors Type – NPN bipolar junction transistor (BJT) Collector-Emitter Voltage (Vceo) – 40 V Collector Current (Ic) – 800 mA (max) Transition Frequency (fT) – ~300 MHz Power Dissipation (Ptot) – 500 mW hFE (DC current gain) – 100–300 typical Package – TO-92 (3-pin) Handy Tips Check the pinout – On the TO-92, with the flat face toward you and legs down, the pins are commonly E-B-C, but always confirm against the datasheet as some variants differ. Switching workhorse – The 2N2222A switches loads up to ~800mA, making it great for driving small relays, LEDs and buzzers from a microcontroller pin. Add a base resistor – Always place a resistor (typically 1k–10k) between your control signal and the base to limit current and protect both the transistor and your driving pin. Amplification too – With its ~300MHz transition frequency it works well in small-signal audio and RF amplifier stages, not just switching. Flyback diode for coils – When switching relays or motors, fit a flyback diode across the coil to clamp back-EMF and protect the transistor. Know the PNP partner – The 2N2907 is the complementary PNP type; handy when building push-pull or H-bridge style circuits. Heat is rarely an issue – At 500mW dissipation it runs cool in most hobby uses, but keep within ratings when switching larger continuous loads.

item.title: 1N5408 Rectifier Diode (3A, 1000V) - 5 Pack
item.description: A convenient 5-pack of the 1N5408 3A, 1000V standard recovery rectifier diode in an axial DO-201AD package — the high-current member of the popular 1N540x family. Ideal for mains-frequency rectification in power supplies, battery chargers and transformer-based circuits where currents up to 3A are expected. Buying in a 5-pack keeps spares on hand for bridge rectifiers and repairs. Spec – Value Pack Quantity – 5 diodes Type – Standard recovery rectifier diode Forward Current (Io) – 3 A Peak Reverse Voltage (Vrrm) – 1000 V Forward Voltage Drop (Vf) – ~1.0 V @ 3 A Reverse Recovery – Standard (not fast) Max Surge Current (Ifsm) – 200 A Package – DO-201AD (axial) Operating Temp – -65 °C to +175 °C Handy Tips High-current workhorse – Rated for 3A versus the 1N400x series' 1A, making it the go-to choice for beefier power supplies and chargers. Mind the polarity – The banded end is the cathode (negative). Fit it backwards in a rectifier and it won't conduct, or it'll fail under reverse voltage. Bridge rectifiers – Four 1N5408s build a robust full-bridge rectifier for transformer supplies up to a few amps — this pack gives you a spare too. Flyback protection – Excellent as a freewheeling diode across relays, solenoids and motors to clamp back-EMF spikes. Not for switching – Standard recovery makes it unsuitable for high-frequency switch-mode supplies; reach for a 1N5819 Schottky or UF400x fast diode there. Derate for heat – Above ~75 °C ambient, reduce the forward current to keep the junction within its temperature limit. Leave the leads long – The axial leads help shed heat; don't crop them too short on continuous high-current loads.

item.title: Aluminum Heatsink 9x9x5mm - IC/Chip Cooling with Thermal Tape (Pack of 5)
item.description: Description Small 9x9x5mm aluminium heatsinks with pre-applied thermal conductive tape, supplied in packs of 5. Ideal for cooling ICs, MOSFETs, voltage regulators, RAM chips, and Raspberry Pi processors to prevent thermal throttling and extend component life. Technical Details / Specs Material Aluminium Dimensions 9 x 9 x 5mm Pack 5 pieces Mounting Pre-applied thermal conductive tape Use IC, RAM, MOS, Raspberry Pi, voltage regulators Handy Tips Clean first: wipe the chip surface clean of dust and oils so the tape bonds well. Peel and press: remove the backing film and press firmly for a few seconds to set the adhesive. Coverage: centre the heatsink over the hottest part of the chip for best heat transfer. Airflow: a little airflow over the fins greatly improves cooling versus still air. Raspberry Pi: fit one to the SoC (and one to the USB/LAN chip) to reduce throttling under load. Reuse: the tape is single-use; replace with fresh thermal tape if you remove a heatsink.

item.title: Pin Header - 40-Pin Single Row 2.54mm, Assorted Colour (Pack of 5)
item.description: Description Single-row 2.54mm pin headers in assorted colours, supplied as a pack of 5x 40-pin strips. Snap to length for breadboards, PCB connections, and electronics prototyping. The colour variety helps with circuit organisation and keying. Technical Details / Specs Pitch 2.54mm Configuration Single row, 1x40 pin Pack 5 strips per pack Colours Assorted (black/white/red/yellow/green/blue) Material Plastic body, metal pins Use Breadboards, PCBs, prototyping Handy Tips Snap to length: break the strip cleanly at the required pin count with pliers or by hand. Colour coding: use different colours to mark power, ground, and signal rows at a glance. Soldering: seat the header in the PCB and tack one end pin first to keep it square. Breadboarding: press headers onto module pads to make them breadboard-friendly. Pitch match: 2.54mm (0.1") is the standard spacing for most perfboard and breadboards. Storage: keep the strips in a small parts box to avoid bending the pins.

item.title: Creality Sermoon P1 All-in-One 3D Scanner
item.description: Creality Sermoon P1 All-in-One 3D Scanner | Live Demo Available in our George Store The Creality Sermoon P1 is a professional handheld blue-laser 3D scanner that scans, processes, and exports – all on the device, with no PC required. Awarded TechRadar Best of CES 2026 , the Sermoon P1 brings industrial-grade accuracy and portability to engineers, makers, designers and reverse-engineering professionals right here on the Garden Route. See it for yourself – we have a live demo unit in-store at Just Colours, George. Come scan a real object and watch the 3D model build on the screen in seconds. Pop in to York Street Boulevard and try it hands-on. Why the Sermoon P1? Most 3D scanners chain you to a laptop. The Sermoon P1 doesn’t. With a Qualcomm processor, 24GB RAM and a 6-inch HD touchscreen built in, you can capture, mesh, edit and export a finished 3D model standing in a workshop, on a factory floor, or out in the field – fully wireless. Specifications Light Source 22 + 7 + 1 blue laser lines + NIR structured light Accuracy Up to 0.02 mm Volumetric Accuracy 0.06 mm/m Scan Speed Up to 100 FPS Scan Range 5×5×5 mm up to 4000×4000×4000 mm Deep-Hole Mode Single-line laser, up to 5:1 depth-to-diameter ratio Processor Qualcomm 8-core CPU, Adreno 740 GPU, 48 TOPS DSP, FPGA Memory / Storage 24GB LPDDR5X RAM / 256GB UFS 4.0 Display 6-inch Full HD touchscreen, 160° viewing angle Connectivity Wi-Fi 7 Battery 2 × 3300 mAh swappable (80% charge in 50 min) Work Modes Standalone / Wired PC / Wireless PC Texture Full-colour RGB camera with Qualcomm ISP Weight 830 g Software Export Compatible with QuickSurface, Geomagic Design X & more Handy Tips – Get the Most From Your Sermoon P1 Markerless NIR mode lets you scan large objects and even the human body with no sticker dots – perfect for quick captures where prep time matters. Deep-hole scanning uses the single-line laser to reach into pipes, recesses and gaps other scanners can’t (tested to 152 mm depth in a 29 mm pipe). No scanning spray needed – the blue laser captures black and shiny metal surfaces straight out the box, saving you mess and consumable cost. Hot-swap your battery mid-scan so a flat cell never ends a session; keep the spare charging on its own USB-C port. Full-colour texture capture means scans come out photo-realistic – ideal for digital archiving, VFX and product visualisation, not just dimensional work. Standalone mode is your friend on-site – capture to the 256GB onboard storage, then transfer over Wi-Fi 7 back at the desk. Export straight into your CAD pipeline – files drop neatly into reverse-engineering and inspection software like Geomagic Design X and QuickSurface. Applications Reverse engineering • Quality inspection • Automotive customisation • Product design • Digital archiving • 3D-print-ready scanning • Heritage & art capture Available now at Just Colours, York Street Boulevard, George. Backed by local support and an in-store demo unit. We ship nationwide across South Africa.

item.title: 7824CT 24V Linear Voltage Regulator (TO-220) - 5 Pack
item.description: 7824CT 24V Linear Voltage Regulator (TO-220) – 5 Pack – Technical Specifications: Module Type – Fixed Linear Voltage Regulator Output Voltage – 24V DC (Fixed) Input Voltage – 27V to 40V DC (Recommended range) Output Current – Up to 1A (with proper heatsinking) Voltage Dropout – ~2V (typical) Regulation Type – Positive Voltage Regulator Package Type – TO-220 Quantity – 5 Units per Pack Output Tolerance – ±4% Quiescent Current – ~5–8mA Protection Features – Thermal Shutdown, Short-Circuit Protection, Safe Area Protection Operating Temperature – 0°C to +125°C (junction) Mounting Type – Through-Hole Pin Configuration – IN (Input), GND (Ground), OUT (Output) Series – 78xx Standard Linear Regulator Family Compatible Applications – Power supplies, embedded systems, analog circuits, industrial equipment Handy Tips for Using the 7824CT Voltage Regulator (5 Pack): 1: This regulator requires the input voltage to be at least ~2V higher than the output (typically 26–30V minimum under load). Supplying less than this will result in unstable or reduced output voltage. 2: This is a linear regulator, meaning it dissipates excess voltage as heat. For example, dropping from 30V to 24V at 1A will generate significant heat. Always use a heatsink when drawing moderate to high current. 3: To ensure stable operation, always include input and output capacitors: Input ~0.33µF (ceramic), Output ~0.1µF to 1µF (ceramic or electrolytic). These reduce noise and prevent oscillation. 4: Each regulator in this 5-pack can be used independently across multiple projects, making it ideal for prototyping, repairs, or bulk builds. 5: The regulator includes built-in protection features, including thermal shutdown and short-circuit protection, but these should not be relied on for normal operation — proper design and heat management are still essential.

item.title: 7812CT 12V Linear Voltage Regulator (TO-220) - 5 Pack
item.description: 7812CT 12V Linear Voltage Regulator (TO-220) – 5 Pack – Technical Specifications: Module Type – Fixed Linear Voltage Regulator Output Voltage – 12V DC (Fixed) Input Voltage – 14V to 27V DC (Recommended range) Output Current – Up to 1A (with proper heatsinking) Voltage Dropout – ~2V (typical) Regulation Type – Positive Voltage Regulator Package Type – TO-220 Quantity – 5 Units per Pack Output Tolerance – ±4% Protection Features – Thermal Shutdown, Short-Circuit Protection, Safe Area Protection Operating Temperature – 0°C to +125°C (junction) Mounting Type – Through-Hole Pin Configuration – IN (Input), GND (Ground), OUT (Output) Series – 78xx Standard Linear Regulator Family Compatible Applications – Relay modules, fans, camera systems, 12V LED strips, embedded systems Handy Tips for Using the 7812CT Voltage Regulator (5 Pack): 1: This 12V regulator requires an input voltage at least ~2V higher than the output — 14V minimum, with 15–18V recommended for stable regulation under load. 2: As a linear regulator it dissipates excess voltage as heat — dropping from 18V to 12V at 1A produces significant heat, so always fit a heatsink for sustained current draws. 3: Always include input (~0.33µF) and output (~0.1–1µF) capacitors close to the IC pins to suppress noise and prevent oscillation. 4: Each regulator in this 5-pack can be used independently across multiple projects — handy for repairs, prototyping, or stocking spares of this commonly used voltage. 5: A very common rail for relay modules, fans, camera systems, and 12V LED strips when stepping down from a higher unregulated supply.

item.title: 7809CT 9V Linear Voltage Regulator (TO-220) - 5 Pack
item.description: 7809CT 9V Linear Voltage Regulator (TO-220) – 5 Pack – Technical Specifications: Module Type – Fixed Linear Voltage Regulator Output Voltage – 9V DC (Fixed) Input Voltage – 11V to 25V DC (Recommended range) Output Current – Up to 1A (with proper heatsinking) Voltage Dropout – ~2V (typical) Regulation Type – Positive Voltage Regulator Package Type – TO-220 Quantity – 5 Units per Pack Output Tolerance – ±4% Protection Features – Thermal Shutdown, Short-Circuit Protection, Safe Area Protection Operating Temperature – 0°C to +125°C (junction) Mounting Type – Through-Hole Pin Configuration – IN (Input), GND (Ground), OUT (Output) Series – 78xx Standard Linear Regulator Family Compatible Applications – Arduino projects, embedded systems, guitar pedals, relay coils, legacy 9V-powered modules Handy Tips for Using the 7809CT Voltage Regulator (5 Pack): 1: This is a fixed 9V regulator from the same 78xx family as the 7805 and 7812 — for stable output, supply at least ~2V higher than the output (11V minimum under load, 12V+ recommended for headroom). 2: As a linear regulator, it dissipates excess input-to-output voltage as heat. Dropping from 12V to 9V at 1A generates noticeable heat — always fit a heatsink for any sustained load above a few hundred mA. 3: Always include input (~0.33µF) and output (~0.1–1µF) capacitors close to the regulator pins to prevent oscillation and reduce noise on the output rail. 4: Each regulator in this 5-pack can be used independently across multiple projects — handy for repairs, prototyping, or stocking spares of this commonly used voltage. 5: Commonly used to derive a clean 9V rail from a 12V supply for guitar pedals, relay coils, and legacy 9V-powered modules.

item.title: 7805CT 5V Linear Voltage Regulator (TO-220) – 5 Pack
item.description: 7805CT 5V Linear Voltage Regulator (TO-220) – 5 Pack – Technical Specifications: Module Type – Fixed Linear Voltage Regulator Output Voltage – 5V DC (Fixed) Input Voltage – 7V to 35V DC (Recommended range) Output Current – Up to 1A (with proper heatsinking) Voltage Dropout – ~2V (typical) Regulation Type – Positive Voltage Regulator Package Type – TO-220 Quantity – 5 Units per Pack Output Tolerance – ±4% Quiescent Current – ~5–8mA Protection Features – Thermal Shutdown, Short-Circuit Protection, Safe Area Protection Operating Temperature – 0°C to +125°C (junction) Mounting Type – Through-Hole Pin Configuration – IN (Input), GND (Ground), OUT (Output) Series – 78xx Standard Linear Regulator Family Compatible Applications – Arduino projects, embedded systems, sensors, breadboard power supplies, DIY electronics Handy Tips for Using the 7805CT Voltage Regulator (5 Pack): 1: The 7805CT provides a stable fixed 5V output, but requires at least ~7V input to regulate properly. Anything lower may result in unstable operation or reduced output voltage. 2: Because this is a linear regulator, excess voltage is converted into heat. Stepping down from 12V to 5V at higher current will generate significant heat — always use a heatsink when drawing more than a few hundred milliamps. 3: For stable and noise-free operation, include decoupling capacitors: Input ~0.33µF, Output ~0.1µF to 1µF. These help prevent oscillation and improve performance. 4: Each regulator in this 5-pack can be used independently across multiple projects, making it ideal for prototyping, repairs, or bulk builds. 5: Built-in thermal shutdown and current limiting provide protection, but should not replace proper design — avoid running the regulator continuously at maximum load without adequate cooling. 6: This IC is perfect for powering microcontrollers, sensors, and logic circuits, delivering a clean and regulated 5V supply.

item.title: 1N5819 Schottky Barrier Rectifier Diode - 5 Pack
item.description: 1N5819 Schottky Barrier Rectifier Diode – 5 Pack – Technical Specifications: Component Type – Schottky Barrier Rectifier Diode Package – DO-41 Through-Hole Quantity – 5 Units per Pack Peak Reverse Voltage – 40V Forward Current – 1A Forward Voltage Drop – ~0.3–0.4V (Low) Reverse Recovery Time – Very Fast (Schottky) Cathode Marking – Stripe Band Handy Tips for Using the 1N5819 Schottky Diode (5 Pack): 1: Schottky diodes have a much lower forward voltage drop (~0.3–0.4V) than standard silicon diodes (~0.7V) — this means less power wasted as heat, making the 1N5819 the preferred choice for efficiency-critical circuits. 2: Commonly used for reverse polarity protection on battery-powered projects — the low forward drop minimises voltage loss compared to a standard diode in the same role. 3: Ideal as a flyback/snubber diode across relay coils and small inductive loads, where its very fast switching helps suppress voltage spikes more effectively than a standard rectifier. 4: The 40V reverse voltage rating means it is suited to low-voltage DC circuits (5V–24V systems) rather than mains-level applications. 5: Each diode in this 5-pack can be used independently across multiple projects — handy for repairs, prototyping, or keeping spares on hand for this widely used component.

item.title: 1N4148 Fast Switching Signal Diode - 5 Pack
item.description: 1N4148 Fast Switching Signal Diode – 5 Pack – Technical Specifications: Component Type – Small Signal Switching Diode Package – DO-35 Through-Hole Quantity – 5 Units per Pack Peak Reverse Voltage – 100V Forward Current – 200mA Reverse Recovery Time – 4ns (Fast Switching) Forward Voltage Drop – ~0.7V Cathode Marking – Stripe Band Handy Tips for Using the 1N4148 Signal Diode (5 Pack): 1: The 1N4148 is a fast-switching signal diode, ideal for logic-level clipping, clamping, and signal protection circuits — it is not rated for mains rectification or high current loads. 2: Its fast 4ns reverse recovery time makes it well suited to high-frequency switching applications where a general-purpose rectifier diode (like the 1N4007) would be too slow. 3: The cathode (negative leg) is marked with a stripe band on the diode body — current flows from anode to cathode when forward biased. 4: A very common choice for protecting GPIO pins from reverse voltage spikes and for use in simple logic-level OR/AND diode gates. 5: Each diode in this 5-pack can be used independently across multiple projects — handy for repairs, prototyping, or keeping spares on hand for this widely used component.

item.title: LM317T Adjustable Voltage Regulator (TO-220) – 5 Pack
item.description: LM317T Adjustable Voltage Regulator (TO-220) – 5 Pack – Technical Specifications: Module Type – Adjustable Linear Voltage Regulator Quantity – 5 Units per Pack Output Voltage – 1.25V to 37V DC (Adjustable) Input Voltage – Up to 40V DC (Maximum) Output Current – Up to 1.5A per regulator (with proper heatsinking) Voltage Dropout – ~2V to 3V (typical) Reference Voltage – 1.25V Regulation Type – Positive Adjustable Regulator Package Type – TO-220 Load Regulation – ~0.1% (typical) Line Regulation – ~0.01% (typical) Protection Features – Thermal Shutdown, Current Limiting, Safe Area Protection Operating Temperature – 0°C to +125°C (junction) Mounting Type – Through-Hole Pin Configuration – ADJ (Adjust), OUT (Output), IN (Input) Adjustment Method – External Resistors (Voltage Set via Divider) Series – LM317 Adjustable Regulator Family Compatible Applications – Variable power supplies, battery chargers, LED drivers, prototyping, DIY electronics Handy Tips for Using the LM317T Adjustable Regulator (5 Pack): 1: The LM317T allows you to set any output voltage between 1.25V and 37V using just two external resistors . A common configuration uses: R1 = 240Ω R2 = variable resistor (potentiometer) to adjust output voltage 2: The regulator requires the input voltage to be at least ~2–3V higher than the desired output voltage . For example, to get 12V output, supply at least 14–15V input. 3: As a linear regulator , the LM317 dissipates excess voltage as heat. At higher currents or large voltage drops, it will generate significant heat — always use a heatsink when needed. 4: Each regulator in this 5-pack can be used independently across multiple projects, making it ideal for prototyping, repairs, or bulk builds. 5: For stable performance, always include capacitors: Input: ~0.1µF Output: ~1µF Optional: Add a capacitor on the ADJ pin (~10µF) for improved ripple rejection 6: Built-in thermal shutdown and current limiting protect the device, but proper thermal design is still essential for long-term reliability. 7: The LM317 can also be used as a current regulator (constant current source), making it useful for LED driving or battery charging applications with a simple resistor configuration. 8: If efficiency is important (e.g., solar or battery systems), consider using a switch-mode (buck) converter , as linear regulators waste power as heat when stepping down voltage.

item.title: BMT LD2410C 24GHz Human Presence mmWave Radar Sensor
item.description: BMT LD2410C 24GHz Human Presence mmWave Radar Sensor – Technical Specifications: Sensor Type – 24GHz FMCW mmWave Radar Manufacturer – Hi-Link (HLK-LD2410C) Operating Frequency – 24.0–24.25GHz (ISM Band) Detection Range – Up to 6m (Motion) / Up to 5m (Static Presence) Distance Resolution – 0.75m Detection Angle – ±60° Detection Type – Movement + Static Presence (Breathing/Micro-Motion) Output – Digital GPIO (3.3V Logic) + UART (256000 baud) Operating Voltage – 5V to 12V DC Connector – 2.54mm Pitch Header (Pre-Soldered) Module Size – 22 × 16mm 1: The key advantage of the LD2410C over a standard PIR sensor is detecting stationary human presence — it can sense the micro-movements of breathing, meaning lights and automations stay active even when someone is sitting still. 2: For simple on/off automations, use the digital OUT pin directly — it outputs a 3.3V HIGH signal when presence is detected and LOW when the area is clear, requiring no additional configuration or microcontroller library. 3: For fine-tuned control, connect via UART (256000 baud) and use the HLKRadarTool configuration software (or the ESPHome ld2410 component) to adjust sensitivity, detection gates, and the unmanned (no-presence) delay time per distance zone. 4: This is the most popular sensor for Home Assistant "room occupancy" automations specifically because it solves the classic PIR problem of lights turning off while someone is sitting motionless at a desk or on a couch. 5: Mount with a clear line of sight to the monitored area — large moving objects such as fans, curtains, or pets within range can occasionally trigger false detections; use the gate sensitivity settings to tune this out for your specific room. 6: Avoid mounting facing glass or highly reflective surfaces at a shallow angle, as reflections can extend or distort the effective detection pattern beyond the intended coverage area.

item.title: BDD MX1616 Dual H-Bridge DC Motor Driver Module
item.description: BDD MX1616 Dual H-Bridge DC Motor Driver Module – Technical Specifications: Driver Type – Dual H-Bridge DC Motor Driver Logic Supply Voltage – 3.3V to 5V Motor Supply Voltage – 4.5V to 36V DC Output Current per Channel – Up to 1.5A (Peak ~2A) Channels – 2 (Independent Direction & Speed Control) Control Interface – PWM + Direction Logic Pins Applications – Robotics, RC Vehicles, Conveyor Systems, Arduino/ESP32 Motor Control 1: This module lets a microcontroller control two DC motors independently — both speed (via PWM) and direction (via logic pins) — without the GPIO pins ever carrying the motor's actual current. 2: Power the module from two separate supplies where possible: logic voltage (3.3V/5V) to the logic VCC pin, and motor voltage (matching your motor's rating) to the motor power input — sharing a common ground between both. 3: Each channel typically uses two direction control pins and one PWM input — setting both direction pins LOW or HIGH together brakes the motor, while opposite states set forward or reverse, and PWM duty cycle controls speed. 4: Stay within the rated continuous current per channel (around 1.5A) — stalled motors draw significantly more current than free-running ones and can overheat the driver if the stall persists. 5: Add adequate ventilation or a small heatsink if running motors near the module's current limit for extended periods, as H-bridge drivers generate heat proportional to current and PWM switching losses.

item.title: 1N4007F 1A 1000V Rectifier Diode
item.description: 1N4007F 1A 1000V Rectifier Diode – Technical Specifications: Component Type – General Purpose Rectifier Diode Package – DO-41 Through-Hole Peak Reverse Voltage – 1000V Forward Current – 1A Peak Forward Surge Current – 30A (8.3ms) Forward Voltage Drop – ~0.7V Cathode Marking – Stripe Band 1: The 1N4007 is the most widely used general-purpose rectifier diode in hobby electronics — a safe default choice for mains rectification, flyback protection, and reverse polarity protection. 2: Its 1000V reverse voltage rating provides a large safety margin in nearly all low-voltage and mains-derived DC circuits, making it a reliable "stock everywhere" component. 3: The most common use is as a flyback/snubber diode across relay coils and solenoids — placed in reverse bias (cathode to positive supply) to absorb the voltage spike generated when the coil is switched off. 4: The cathode (negative leg) is marked with a stripe band on the body — always verify orientation before soldering, especially in rectifier bridge configurations. 5: For higher current loads (above 1A), step up to the 1N5408 (3A); for fast signal-level switching, use the 1N4148 instead.

item.title: 1N5819 Schottky Barrier Rectifier Diode
item.description: 1N5819 Schottky Barrier Rectifier Diode – Technical Specifications: Component Type – Schottky Barrier Rectifier Diode Package – DO-41 Through-Hole Peak Reverse Voltage – 40V Forward Current – 1A Forward Voltage Drop – ~0.3–0.4V (Low) Reverse Recovery Time – Very Fast (Schottky) Cathode Marking – Stripe Band 1: Schottky diodes have a much lower forward voltage drop (~0.3–0.4V) than standard silicon diodes (~0.7V) — this means less power wasted as heat, making the 1N5819 the preferred choice for efficiency-critical circuits. 2: Commonly used for reverse polarity protection on battery-powered projects — the low forward drop minimises voltage loss compared to a standard diode in the same role. 3: Ideal as a flyback/snubber diode across relay coils and small inductive loads, where its very fast switching helps suppress voltage spikes more effectively than a standard rectifier. 4: The 40V reverse voltage rating means it is suited to low-voltage DC circuits (5V–24V systems) rather than mains-level applications. 5: The cathode (negative leg) is marked with a stripe band — always check orientation before soldering, especially in reverse-protection circuits where polarity is critical.

item.title: 1N4148 Fast Switching Signal Diode
item.description: 1N4148 Fast Switching Signal Diode – Technical Specifications: Component Type – Small Signal Switching Diode Package – DO-35 Through-Hole Peak Reverse Voltage – 100V Forward Current – 200mA Reverse Recovery Time – 4ns (Fast Switching) Forward Voltage Drop – ~0.7V Cathode Marking – Stripe Band 1: The 1N4148 is a fast-switching signal diode, ideal for logic-level clipping, clamping, and signal protection circuits — it is not rated for mains rectification or high current loads. 2: Its fast 4ns reverse recovery time makes it well suited to high-frequency switching applications where a general-purpose rectifier diode (like the 1N4007) would be too slow. 3: The cathode (negative leg) is marked with a stripe band on the diode body — current flows from anode to cathode when forward biased. 4: A very common choice for protecting GPIO pins from reverse voltage spikes and for use in simple logic-level OR/AND diode gates. 5: For power rectification or higher current handling, use the 1N4007 (1A) or 1N5408 (3A) instead — the 1N4148 is strictly a signal-level component.

item.title: 7812CT 12V Linear Voltage Regulator (TO-220)
item.description: 7812CT 12V Linear Voltage Regulator (TO-220) – Technical Specifications: Module Type – Fixed Linear Voltage Regulator Output Voltage – 12V DC (Fixed) Input Voltage – 14V to 27V DC (Recommended range) Output Current – Up to 1A (with proper heatsinking) Voltage Dropout – ~2V (typical) Package Type – TO-220 Output Tolerance – ±4% Protection Features – Thermal Shutdown, Short-Circuit Protection, Safe Area Protection Pin Configuration – IN (Input), GND (Ground), OUT (Output) Series – 78xx Standard Linear Regulator Family 1: This 12V regulator requires an input voltage at least ~2V higher than the output — 14V minimum, with 15–18V recommended for stable regulation under load. 2: As a linear regulator it dissipates excess voltage as heat — dropping from 18V to 12V at 1A produces significant heat, so always fit a heatsink for sustained current draws. 3: Always include input (~0.33µF) and output (~0.1–1µF) capacitors close to the IC pins to suppress noise and prevent oscillation. 4: A very common rail for relay modules, fans, camera systems, and 12V LED strips when stepping down from a higher unregulated supply. 5: Built-in thermal shutdown and short-circuit protection are safety nets only — proper heatsinking and current limiting in your design remain essential for long-term reliability.

item.title: 7809CT 9V Linear Voltage Regulator (TO-220)
item.description: 7809CT 9V Linear Voltage Regulator (TO-220) – Technical Specifications: Module Type – Fixed Linear Voltage Regulator Output Voltage – 9V DC (Fixed) Input Voltage – 11V to 25V DC (Recommended range) Output Current – Up to 1A (with proper heatsinking) Voltage Dropout – ~2V (typical) Package Type – TO-220 Output Tolerance – ±4% Protection Features – Thermal Shutdown, Short-Circuit Protection, Safe Area Protection Pin Configuration – IN (Input), GND (Ground), OUT (Output) Series – 78xx Standard Linear Regulator Family 1: This is a fixed 9V regulator from the same 78xx family as the 7805 and 7812 — for stable output, supply at least ~2V higher than the output (11V minimum under load, 12V+ recommended for headroom). 2: As a linear regulator, it dissipates excess input-to-output voltage as heat. Dropping from 12V to 9V at 1A generates noticeable heat — always fit a heatsink for any sustained load above a few hundred mA. 3: Always include input (~0.33µF) and output (~0.1–1µF) capacitors close to the regulator pins to prevent oscillation and reduce noise on the output rail. 4: Built-in thermal shutdown and short-circuit protection are safety nets, not substitutes for proper heatsinking and circuit design under normal operating conditions. 5: Commonly used to derive a clean 9V rail from a 12V supply for guitar pedals, relay coils, and legacy 9V-powered modules.

item.title: W04F 1.5A 400V Bridge Rectifier Diode (4-Pin DIP)
item.description: W04F 1.5A 400V Bridge Rectifier Diode (4-Pin DIP) – Technical Specifications: Component Type – Single-Phase Bridge Rectifier Package – 4-Pin DIP (W04 style) Peak Repetitive Reverse Voltage (VRRM) – 400V Average Forward Current (Io) – 1.5A Peak Forward Surge Current – 50A (8.3ms) Forward Voltage Drop – ~1.2V per leg Pin Configuration – AC, AC, +, – Operating Temperature – -55°C to +150°C 1: A bridge rectifier converts AC voltage into pulsating DC by routing both halves of the AC waveform through the diode bridge. Connect your transformer secondary or AC source to the two pins marked "~" (AC), and take your DC output from "+" and "–". 2: Always add a smoothing capacitor (typically 1000µF–4700µF electrolytic) across the + and – output to convert the pulsating DC into smooth DC suitable for powering electronics. 3: The 400V rating refers to the maximum reverse voltage the bridge can block — for mains-derived supplies this provides a generous safety margin, but never exceed the rated 1.5A average current. 4: Bridge rectifiers run warm under load — for currents approaching the 1.5A limit, ensure the PCB has adequate copper area or add a small heatsink to the package for long-term reliability. 5: Always double check pin orientation before powering up — reversing the AC and DC connections will not damage the bridge itself but will result in no usable DC output.

item.title: 2N2222A NPN General Purpose Transistor (TO-92)
item.description: 2N2222A NPN General Purpose Transistor (TO-92) – Technical Specifications: Component Type – NPN Bipolar Junction Transistor Package – TO-92 Through-Hole Collector-Emitter Voltage (Vceo) – 40V Collector Current (Continuous) – 600mA Power Dissipation – 625mW DC Current Gain (hFE) – 100–300 Transition Frequency – 300MHz Pin Order (flat face forward) – Emitter / Base / Collector 1: The 2N2222A switches current from Collector to Emitter based on a small Base current. Always use a Base resistor between your GPIO pin and the Base — 1kΩ for 5V logic, 330–470Ω for 3.3V logic (ESP8266/ESP32). 2: To use it as a clean ON/OFF switch, drive it into saturation by ensuring base current is at least 1/10th of the load current — under-driving wastes power as heat instead of switching cleanly. 3: When switching inductive loads such as relay coils or small motors, always add a flyback diode (e.g. 1N4007) across the load in reverse bias to protect the transistor from voltage spikes. 4: TO-92 pinout can vary by manufacturer — always verify Emitter/Base/Collector order against the datasheet before wiring, especially before committing to a PCB layout. 5: Rated for 600mA continuous — for higher current loads, step up to a TIP31C or a logic-level MOSFET such as the IRLZ44N.

item.title: LM317T Adjustable Voltage Regulator (TO-220)
item.description: LM317T Adjustable Voltage Regulator (TO-220) – Technical Specifications: Module Type – Adjustable Linear Voltage Regulator Output Voltage – 1.25V to 37V DC (Adjustable) Input Voltage – Up to 40V DC (Maximum) Output Current – Up to 1.5A (with proper heatsinking) Voltage Dropout – ~2V to 3V (typical) Reference Voltage – 1.25V Regulation Type – Positive Adjustable Regulator Package Type – TO-220 Load Regulation – ~0.1% (typical) Line Regulation – ~0.01% (typical) Protection Features – Thermal Shutdown, Current Limiting, Safe Area Protection Operating Temperature – 0°C to +125°C (junction) Mounting Type – Through-Hole Pin Configuration – ADJ (Adjust), OUT (Output), IN (Input) Adjustment Method – External Resistors (Voltage Set via Divider) Series – LM317 Adjustable Regulator Family Compatible Applications – Variable power supplies, battery chargers, LED drivers, prototyping, DIY electronics Handy Tips for Using the LM317T Adjustable Regulator: 1: The LM317T allows you to set any output voltage between 1.25V and 37V using just two external resistors . A common configuration uses: R1 = 240Ω R2 = variable resistor (potentiometer) to adjust output voltage 2: The regulator requires the input voltage to be at least ~2–3V higher than the desired output voltage . For example, to get 12V output, supply at least 14–15V input. 3: As a linear regulator , the LM317 dissipates excess voltage as heat. At higher currents or large voltage drops, it will generate significant heat — always use a heatsink when needed. 4: This regulator is ideal for building adjustable power supplies, battery chargers, LED drivers, and prototyping circuits where variable voltage is required. 5: For stable performance, always include capacitors: Input: ~0.1µF Output: ~1µF Optional: Add a capacitor on the ADJ pin (~10µF) for improved ripple rejection 6: Built-in thermal shutdown and current limiting protect the device, but proper thermal design is still essential for long-term reliability. 7: The LM317 can also be used as a current regulator (constant current source), making it useful for LED driving or battery charging applications with a simple resistor configuration. 8: If efficiency is important (e.g., solar or battery systems), consider using a switch-mode (buck) converter , as linear regulators waste power as heat when stepping down voltage.

item.title: 7805CT 5V Linear Voltage Regulator (TO-220)
item.description: 7805CT 5V Linear Voltage Regulator (TO-220) – Technical Specifications: Module Type – Fixed Linear Voltage Regulator Output Voltage – 5V DC (Fixed) Input Voltage – 7V to 35V DC (Recommended range) Output Current – Up to 1A (with proper heatsinking) Voltage Dropout – ~2V (typical) Regulation Type – Positive Voltage Regulator Package Type – TO-220 Output Tolerance – ±4% Quiescent Current – ~5–8mA Protection Features – Thermal Shutdown, Short-Circuit Protection, Safe Area Protection Operating Temperature – 0°C to +125°C (junction) Mounting Type – Through-Hole Pin Configuration – IN (Input), GND (Ground), OUT (Output) Series – 78xx Standard Linear Regulator Family Compatible Applications – Arduino projects, embedded systems, sensors, breadboard power supplies, DIY electronics Handy Tips for Using the 7805CT Voltage Regulator: 1: The 7805CT provides a stable fixed 5V output , but requires at least ~7V input to regulate properly. Anything lower may result in unstable operation or reduced output voltage. 2: Because this is a linear regulator , excess voltage is converted into heat. For example, stepping down from 12V to 5V at higher current will generate significant heat — always use a heatsink when drawing more than a few hundred milliamps. 3: For stable and noise-free operation, include decoupling capacitors : Input: ~0.33µF Output: ~0.1µF to 1µF These help prevent oscillation and improve performance. 4: This regulator is a drop-in replacement for any 7805-based circuit — commonly used for repairs, prototyping, and powering 5V logic and microcontrollers from a higher voltage supply. 5: Built-in thermal shutdown and current limiting provide protection, but should not replace proper design — avoid running the regulator continuously at maximum load without adequate cooling. 6: This IC is perfect for powering microcontrollers, sensors, and logic circuits , delivering a clean and regulated 5V supply. 7: If efficiency is important (e.g., battery-powered systems), consider using a buck converter , as linear regulators lose excess power as heat.

item.title: 7824CT 24V Linear Voltage Regulator (TO-220)
item.description: 7824CT 24V Linear Voltage Regulator (TO-220) – Technical Specifications: Module Type – Fixed Linear Voltage Regulator Output Voltage – 24V DC (Fixed) Input Voltage – 27V to 40V DC (Recommended range) Output Current – Up to 1A (with proper heatsinking) Voltage Dropout – ~2V (typical) Regulation Type – Positive Voltage Regulator Package Type – TO-220 Output Tolerance – ±4% Quiescent Current – ~5–8mA Protection Features – Thermal Shutdown, Short-Circuit Protection, Safe Area Protection Operating Temperature – 0°C to +125°C (junction) Mounting Type – Through-Hole Pin Configuration – IN (Input), GND (Ground), OUT (Output) Series – 78xx Standard Linear Regulator Family Compatible Applications – Power supplies, embedded systems, analog circuits, industrial control Handy Tips for Using the 7824CT Voltage Regulator: 1: The 7824CT provides a stable fixed 24V output , but requires the input voltage to be at least ~2V higher than the output (typically 26–30V minimum under load). Supplying less than this will result in unstable or reduced output voltage. 2: This is a linear regulator , meaning it dissipates excess voltage as heat. For example, dropping from 30V to 24V at 1A will generate significant heat. Always use a heatsink when drawing moderate to high current. 3: To ensure stable operation, always include input and output capacitors : Input: ~0.33µF (ceramic) Output: ~0.1µF to 1µF (ceramic or electrolytic) These reduce noise and prevent oscillation. 4: The regulator includes built-in protection features , including thermal shutdown and short-circuit protection, but these should not be relied on for normal operation — proper design and heat management are still essential. 5: The TO-220 package allows easy mounting to a heatsink — use thermal paste and an insulating kit if mounting to grounded metal surfaces to avoid electrical shorts. 6: This IC is ideal for clean, low-noise 24V rails , but not efficient for large voltage drops. For higher efficiency power conversion, consider using a DC-DC buck converter instead.
